about: One row per JSON-RPC method the dispatcher answers. The set of `method` values must equal the dispatcher's match table exactly (test/qa_registry_test.dart fails otherwise), so a method cannot ship without a row. `class` decides what the harness is allowed to do: pure/read/sandbox run for real against an isolated data dir; mutating/network/desktop only run a refusal case, or carry a `skip` reason.

classes.pure: No OS state is read or written. Runs for real.
classes.read: Reads OS or DB state, writes nothing. Runs for real.
classes.sandbox: Would write, but only inside the isolated data dir the harness creates. Runs for real.
classes.mutating: Changes this machine (firewall, registry, hosts, services, files outside the sandbox). Only a refusal case runs, or it is skipped with a reason.
classes.network: Sends a request off the machine. Never runs here.
classes.desktop: Shows UI on the interactive desktop. Never runs here.

The scan schedule (D-027): enabled, interval_hours, target, last_started and next_due. Off by default in the isolated settings file, so the pinned case is the off state; the timer itself is proven by the engine's own unit tests and by `scripts\verify-scan-schedule.ps1`.

Validated and persisted into the isolated settings.json. The engine checks that the value is a language tag, not that it is in a fixed list: the UI owns the packs, so a language added next month must not need an engine change.

Outbound traffic, and not only when the user configured a URL: with nothing saved the engine falls back to the channel's compiled-in feed (D-046, engine\src\settings.rs), so a sandbox with an empty data dir still reaches github.com. This row was classed `read` on the belief that an unconfigured engine answers `disabled` and stays silent - that belief was false, and on 2026-11-12 the case was the one red case in a `-Tier full` run (a DNS failure, and a 404 either way: the published v0.1.0 carries no update.json). The update path is measured against a local feed by scripts\verify-update.ps1; what the *published* feed answers is what docs\TODO.md 0.6 row 1 checks against a release.

Reads the reports the engine wrote for panics, unclean exits and hangs (the last one filed by the watchdog thread when the runtime's heartbeat stops). Empty is the healthy answer, and it is read from the isolated data dir, so the harness never sees this machine's real reports.
A report id is validated before it is turned into a path, so `..\..\settings.json` cannot be asked for; an unknown id is an error rather than an empty object.
Removing a report that does not exist answers deleted=false (idempotent, like job.cancel). It only ever touches the reports directory.
